jobs.title: Senior FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
Lead the Future of Dentistry. 

Overjet is the world-leader in dental AI. Already, thousands of dental providers and insurers rely on our platform to deliver the best possible care. Now, we’re looking for talented people to fulfill our mission: improve oral health for all.

Overjet is where builders become leaders. Everyone here loves to make new things: new products, new partnerships, new content, and a new category of AI technology. And as Overjet grows ridiculously fast, so will you.

Simply put, there’s no better place to accelerate your career. Come join us!

The Role
Overjet is scaling fast — and this role sits at the center of that growth. As a key member of the Finance Team, you will play a central role in our FP&A function, supporting financial planning, reporting, and analysis across the business — reporting to our Senior Director of FP&A. You'll love this job if you're someone who thrives at the intersection of rigorous financial modeling and real business partnership — someone who can build a model from scratch in the morning and walk a business leader through a forecast review in the afternoon with equal confidence. This is an incredible opportunity to help lead the future of dental care — by shaping the financial foundation that drives Overjet's next stage of growth, with direct exposure to board-level reporting and our annual operating budget process.


Responsibilities

 - Own the ARR model and revenue forecasting process, partnering closely with GTM leadership to build and maintain accurate, insight-driven projections

 - Lead the End of Year GTM budget process, coordinating across Sales, Customer Success, and Finance to produce a bottoms-up plan

 - Manage department-level operational expenses, partnering with business owners to track budgets, flag variances, and drive accountability across the organization

 - Own the monthly commission calculation process, ensuring accurate and timely payouts in close partnership with Sales leadership and People Operations

 - Drive monthly and quarterly business reviews, translating complex financial data into clear narratives for senior leadership and board-level audiences

 - Prepare monthly and quarterly investor data requests

 - Prepare board materials and executive presentations that communicate financial performance, trends, and strategic implications with clarity and precision

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field

 - 6+ years of experience in FP&A, investment banking, or Private Equity/ Venture 

 - Experience in a SaaS or high-growth technology environment, with fluency in ARR metrics, SaaS KPIs, and financial planning best practices

 - Familiarity with variable commission plans and sales concepts

 - Demonstrated ability to build and influence relationships with cross-functional stakeholders across GTM, Operations, and G&A functions

 - Strong ability to communicate complex financial concepts clearly to leadership

 - Proficiency with Pigment or similar forecasting tool; experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, and AI productivity tools a strong plus

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, technical, and mission-focused environment

jobs.title: Dental Customer Success Manager- Egypt/ Pakistan
jobs.description:
Lead the Future of Dentistry.

Overjet is the world-leader in dental AI. Already, thousands of dental providers and insurers rely on our platform to deliver the best possible care. Now, we’re looking for talented people to fulfill our mission: improve oral health for all.

Overjet is where builders become leaders. Everyone here loves to make new things: new products, new partnerships, new content, and a new category of AI technology. And as Overjet grows ridiculously fast, so will you.

Simply put, there’s no better place to accelerate your career. Come join us!

The Role

Private practice dentists don't trust software vendors easily, and they especially don't trust anyone telling them how to run clinical decisions who doesn't actually understand dentistry. That's the gap this role closes. You'll own a book of SMB (private practice) accounts across the US, and you'll need real dental knowledge to have a credible conversation about diagnostic AI, not just a script. Without that grounding, adoption stalls, renewals slip, and practices quietly churn because nobody earned the right to keep them engaged.

You'll sit within our Customer Success and Support org, working closely with Support, Product, and Engineering, but the relationship, the health of the account, and the outcome all sit with you. You're also operating without a fully built playbook in a startup that moves fast, so you'll be building your own approach to a given account more often than following an existing one.

If earning a skeptical clinician's trust and turning that into real product adoption sounds like the fun part of the job rather than a slog, keep reading.

Responsibilities

 - Onboard new customers, guiding them through setup, training, and best practices to ensure successful adoption of the platform.

 - Build and maintain strong customer relationships, serving as the primary point of contact to understand goals, challenges, and usage patterns.

 - Proactively monitor customer health and engagement, identifying risks and opportunities to improve retention and expansion.

 - Provide product expertise and troubleshooting support, collaborating with support, product, and engineering teams to resolve issues efficiently.

 - Gather customer feedback and advocate internally, helping influence product improvements and ensuring the customer voice is represented across the organization.

Qualifications

You need real dental knowledge: the first step of our application process is built to test for it directly. That knowledge might come from being a currently practicing dentist, a dental hygienist, a dental school graduate, or someone with hands-on clinical training, but it has to be real and current enough to hold a credible conversation with a skeptical dentist about their own workflow. From there, we care about whether you can own a relationship end to end and move a customer from tolerating a product to actively using it. Prior Customer Success Management or B2B SaaS experience, especially owning a high volume book of accounts, is a genuine plus and will make ramping faster, but it's optional. If you don't have real dental knowledge, this role isn't a fit no matter how strong your customer success background is.

 - Education: Dental training or clinical background (dentist, dental hygienist, or equivalent) is required. 

 - Skills: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, exceptional organizational skills, strong product troubleshooting instincts

 - Experience: 3+ years of professional work experience. B2B SaaS or CSM book-of-business ownership preferred but not required


PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS ROLE WILL BE PAID IN USD.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager, Mid-Market
jobs.description:
Lead the Future of Dentistry. 

Overjet is the world-leader in dental AI. Already, thousands of dental providers and insurers rely on our platform to deliver the best possible care. Now, we’re looking for talented people to fulfill our mission: improve oral health for all.

Overjet is where builders become leaders. Everyone here loves to make new things: new products, new partnerships, new content, and a new category of AI technology. And as Overjet grows ridiculously fast, so will you.

Simply put, there’s no better place to accelerate your career. Come join us!

The Mission and the Hard Part

A mid-market dental practice doesn't decide to trust Overjet with their standard of care because of a sales pitch. They decide during the pilot, watching whether the platform actually earns a place in how their office runs day to day. If that pilot doesn't land, the deal doesn't expand, and it might not renew at all. You'll sit on our Customer Success team, owning the relationship with mid-market accounts (mostly dental office leadership and central office decision makers) from the moment the pilot starts through renewal and expansion.

There's no single stakeholder to win over here. A dentist, a hygienist, a front desk manager, and a central office administrator each need their own reason to actually use the platform, and getting the whole office bought in, not just the person who signed the contract, is the job. If turning a lukewarm or skeptical pilot into a practice that expands and renews sounds like a fun puzzle rather than an uphill grind, keep reading.

What You'll Own

 - You will own the pilot outcome for every mid-market account you're assigned, which means proving Overjet's value fast enough that practices choose to expand instead of churning at the end of the trial.

 - You will own the relationship across the whole office, not just the signer, which means getting dentists, hygienists, and front-office staff (the "total office") genuinely using the platform, not just tolerating it.

 - You will own expansion and upsell targets for your book of accounts, which means proactively spotting low-usage accounts and building a plan to turn them around before they become churn risks.

 - You will own the account review cadence, which means running regular in-person and phone check-ins that surface real satisfaction and utilization signals, not just checking a box on a schedule.

 - You will own improvements to how we onboard and implement new mid-market accounts, which means flagging what's broken in account setup and training and fixing it, not just running the process as it exists today.

What Makes the Right Candidate Keep Reading

You should already know what it takes to keep a B2B SaaS account renewing and expanding, ideally with real experience turning renewals and upsells into a repeatable motion rather than just responding when something breaks. This role rewards someone who's genuinely curious about dentistry, insurance, and AI, and who gets energy from convincing a busy dental office to change how they work, instead of waiting for them to come around on their own. You'll be managing several accounts at once with real numbers attached to expansion and usage, so we need the process discipline to keep it all straight and the hustle to go the extra mile when an account needs it. If you want a role where relationship-building and hustle are the job itself, not a distraction from it, this is a good fit. If you're looking for a support seat where success means closing tickets rather than growing accounts, this probably isn't it.

 - Education: Bachelor's degree preferred, but substantial relevant experience is a fine substitute

 - Skills: Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with comfort working cross-functionally across dental office staff and internal teams
